Order No.04/09.05.2025 I.A. No.5921 of 2025 This Criminal Appeal (SJ) has been filed on behalf of the appellants by challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 20.12.2024 passed in R.C. Case No.07(A)/1998-R CNR-JHRN01-000025-1998 (FIR-no-R.C. 07(A) 1998-R)
passed by Sri Prabhat Kumar Sharma, learned A.J.C.-XVIII Cum Spl. Judge CBI, Ranchi by which the appellants have been convicted for the offences under Sections 120(B) R/W, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for three (03) years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- each.

2. I.A. No. 5921 of 2025 has been filed on behalf of the appellants for confirmation of provisional bail which has been granted by learned Trial Court vide order dated 20.12.2024 by Sri Prabhat Kumar Sharma, learned Spl. Judge, CBI Ranchi.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the appellants had moved before the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide SLP No.6210 of 2025 which has been disposed of vide order dated 28.04.2025 with liberty to file fresh application for bail before the High Court in accordance with law.

4. It appears that the order dated 28.04.2025 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court reads as follows:-
Pramod Kumar @ Pramod Kumar Roi vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25481459/
1 "The petitioners have been convicted under Sections 420,467,468,471, read with Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 03 years.

sentences.text: The petitioners were granted interim bail by the trial court on 20.12.2024 initially for a period of 45 days, which was extended on 31.01.2025 till 14.02.2025.

although the appeal was filed before the High Court within time, but since it came to the court after extended period i.e. after 14.02.2025,
the High Court declined to extend the bail.
Learned counsel may move a fresh application for bail before the High Court in accordance with law.
In the meanwhile, the interim bail shall be deemed to be extended for a further period of four weeks from today.
In view of above, the Special Leave Petitioner is disposed of.

Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of."
5.
Learned Spl.PP has not opposed the prayer for confirmation of provisional bail.

6. Having heard learned counsel for both the sides and considering the facts of this case, it appears that the appellants had been granted Provisional Bail vide dated 30.01.2024 by the learned Trial Court till 14.02.2025.

7. Under the circumstances and in view of the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Provisional Bail granted to the appellants namely Pramod Kumar @ Pramod Kumar Roi and Vinod Kumar @ Binod Kumar @ Vinod Kumar Singh the learned Court below is hereby confirmed.

2. I.A. No. 5921 of 2025 has been filed on behalf of the appellants for confirmation of provisional bail which has been granted by learned Trial Court vide order dated 20.12.2024 by Sri Prabhat Kumar Sharma, learned Spl. Judge, CBI Ranchi.
4. It appears that the order dated 28.04.2025 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court reads as follows:-
Pramod Kumar @ Pramod Kumar Roi vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25481459/
1 "The petitioners have been convicted under Sections 420,467,468,471, read with Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 03 years.
The petitioners were granted interim bail by the trial court on 20.12.2024 initially for a period of 45 days, which was extended on 31.01.2025 till 14.02.2025.
although the appeal was filed before the High Court within time, but since it came to the court after extended period i.e. after 14.02.2025,
the High Court declined to extend the bail.
Learned counsel may move a fresh application for bail before the High Court in accordance with law.
In the meanwhile, the interim bail shall be deemed to be extended for a further period of four weeks from today.
In view of above, the Special Leave Petitioner is disposed of.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of."
5.
6. Having heard learned counsel for both the sides and considering the facts of this case, it appears that the appellants had been granted Provisional Bail vide dated 30.01.2024 by the learned Trial Court till 14.02.2025.
7. Under the circumstances and in view of the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Provisional Bail granted to the appellants namely Pramod Kumar @ Pramod Kumar Roi and Vinod Kumar @ Binod Kumar @ Vinod Kumar Singh the learned Court below is hereby confirmed.
8. This I.A. No.5921 of 2025 is stands allowed and disposed of.
